Low-dose rivaroxaban with aspirin in vascular disease

Does adding low-dose rivaroxaban to antiplatelet therapy reduce major vascular events? Four trials ask versions of this and their registered primary endpoints are not the same endpoint.

What was measured

Table 4. What was measured
Comparatoraspirin alone or placebo, depending on the trial
Estimandtime to first event — random-effects
Effect scalereported on the log scale; nothing is pooled on this outcome

Pooled result

Estimate withdrawn. THE FOUR TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT, AND TWO OF THEM DIFFER FROM THE OTHERS IN WAYS THE REGISTRY STATES EXPLICITLY. VOYAGER PAD'S PRIMARY CARRIES TWO WHOLE COMPONENTS THAT APPEAR IN NO OTHER TRIAL HERE. Verbatim: 'Composite of Myocardial Infarction (MI), Ischemic Stroke, Cardiovascular Death, ACUTE LIMB ISCHEMIA (ALI) AND MAJOR AMPUTATION DUE TO A VASCULAR ETIOLOGY' -- five components. COMPASS's is 'Myocardial Infarction (MI), Stroke, or Cardiovascular (CV) Death' and ATLAS ACS 2's is 'Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction, or Stroke': three each, with no limb outcome at all. Acute limb ischaemia and major amputation are not rare in a post-revascularisation peripheral-artery population; they are much of what that trial was counting. AND COMMANDER HF COUNTS A DIFFERENT DEATH. Its registered primary is 'Event Rate of ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY, Myocardial Infarction (MI), or Stroke'. COMPASS and ATLAS count CARDIOVASCULAR death. All-cause mortality in a decompensated-heart-failure population includes a great many deaths an antithrombotic cannot prevent, and pooling it with a cardiovascular-death composite averages two different questions. COMMANDER HF ALSO REGISTERS A RATE RATHER THAN A COUNT: 'Event Rate / (100 pt-yr) = 100*n/(total risk exposure)'. That is why this page holds no event counts for it, and none for ATLAS ACS 2, whose primary is registered as a PERCENTAGE of patients analysed WHILE ON TREATMENT. SEPARATELY: THE POPULATIONS ARE NOT ONE POPULATION -- stable coronary or peripheral artery disease; peripheral artery disease immediately after lower-extremity revascularisation; heart failure with coronary disease after decompensation; and recent acute coronary syndrome. That alone would not withdraw an estimate, and it is recorded because it is the reason the endpoints differ.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED, STATED AS PROMINENTLY AS WHAT IS WRONG. (1) THE ARITHMETIC IS RIGHT. Pooling the four published hazard ratios by DerSimonian-Laird gives 0.8494 (0.7775 to 0.9278), which is the card's 0.85 (0.77 to 0.94) to within rounding. Nothing here was miscomputed; what was averaged should not have been. (2) THE TRIAL IDENTITIES ARE CORRECT and every arm size matches its registration. (3) THE DIRECTION IS CONSISTENT ACROSS ALL FOUR, and that is worth saying plainly because a withdrawal should not leave a reader with less than they had. COMPASS 0.76 (0.66 to 0.86), VOYAGER PAD 0.85 (0.76 to 0.96), ATLAS ACS 2 0.84 (0.72 to 0.97) and COMMANDER HF 0.94 (0.84 to 1.05). Three of the four exclude no effect; all four point the same way. Every one is on this page. WHAT THIS WITHDRAWAL DOES NOT ESTABLISH: NOT that rivaroxaban is ineffective in vascular disease, and not that no synthesis of these trials is possible. It establishes that THESE FOUR ENDPOINTS ARE NOT ONE ENDPOINT, so a single pooled hazard ratio over them does not estimate a quantity any of the four trials measured. A NOTE ON THE PUBLISHED COMPARISON, per this repository's own queue item 17: the benchmark database's only entry for this outcome is COMPASS itself, Eikelboom 2017, HR 0.76 (0.66 to 0.86) -- AND COMPASS IS ONE OF THE INCLUDED TRIALS. A benchmark that shares a registration with an included trial is not an independent comparison. Here it at least does not agree with the pooled value, so nothing was falsely corroborated; on BEMPEDOIC_ACID the same configuration produced perfect agreement with itself. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS IDENTIFIED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: the three trials whose composites genuinely share components -- COMPASS, ATLAS ACS 2 and, if its all-cause death component is accepted, COMMANDER HF -- could be synthesised without VOYAGER's limb outcomes. Choosing which of those is an estimand decision, and its answer is computable from the values already on this page. PARKED.

Major vascular events, as each trial defines them. These 4 trials are NOT pooled, and the reason is stated rather than the outcome being quietly omitted: THE FOUR TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT, AND TWO OF THEM DIFFER FROM THE OTHERS IN WAYS THE REGISTRY STATES EXPLICITLY. VOYAGER PAD'S PRIMARY CARRIES TWO WHOLE COMPONENTS THAT APPEAR IN NO OTHER TRIAL HERE. COMPASS's is 'Myocardial Infarction (MI), Stroke, or Cardiovascular (CV) Death' and ATLAS ACS 2's is 'Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction, or Stroke': three each, with no limb outcome at all. Acute limb ischaemia and major amputation are not rare in a post-revascularisation peripheral-artery population; they are much of what that trial was counting. AND COMMANDER HF COUNTS A DIFFERENT DEATH. Its registered primary is 'Event Rate of ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY, Myocardial Infarction (MI), or Stroke'. COMPASS and ATLAS count CARDIOVASCULAR death. All-cause mortality in a decompensated-heart-failure population includes a great many deaths an antithrombotic cannot prevent, and pooling it with a cardiovascular-death composite averages two different questions. COMMANDER HF ALSO REGISTERS A RATE RATHER THAN A COUNT: 'Event Rate / (100 pt-yr) = 100*n/(total risk exposure)'. That is why this page holds no event counts for it, and none for ATLAS ACS 2, whose primary is registered as a PERCENTAGE of patients analysed WHILE ON TREATMENT. SEPARATELY: THE POPULATIONS ARE NOT ONE POPULATION -- stable coronary or peripheral artery disease; peripheral artery disease immediately after lower-extremity revascularisation; heart failure with coronary disease after decompensation; and recent acute coronary syndrome. That alone would not withdraw an estimate, and it is recorded because it is the reason the endpoints differ.1
